topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Mutations, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can generate cancer through clonal evolution and why cells differ in their susceptibility to that process.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how strongly environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being an unavoidable consequence of bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the cooperation between pathogens and oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and how the body's handling of an exposure determines its mutagenic effects.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a separate promotional stimulus before tumours develop.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on the biological context of exposure and consolidate that principle within the preceding account of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Evidence linking human carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of assessing them to frame everyday risk–benefit decisions.
